question: A patient with recurrent iridocyclitis develops 360° posterior synechiae (seclusio pupillae). Slit-lamp examination shows a tent-shaped, forward-bowing iris and elevated intraocular pressure. Which mechanism best explains the raised IOP?

answers.text: Trabecular meshwork obstruction by inflammatory cells in the open angle

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While trabeculitis does occur in iridocyclitis, this scenario describes a structural complication — 360° posterior synechiae — which causes iris bombé, a separate and distinct mechanism of raised IOP.

answers.text: Aqueous accumulation behind the iris due to blockade of pupillary flow, causing forward iris bowing (iris bombé) and secondary angle closure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. When 360° posterior synechiae (seclusio pupillae) form, aqueous produced by the ciliary body cannot pass through the pupil to reach the anterior chamber. Pressure builds behind the iris, bowing it forward (iris bombé), narrowing or closing the angle — a secondary angle-closure mechanism requiring peripheral iridectomy or laser iridotomy.

answers.text: Steroid-induced elevation of IOP from long-term topical corticosteroid use

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Steroid-induced glaucoma is a valid complication of treatment, but it does not produce a tent-shaped forward-bowing iris. The physical sign of iris bombé points to a mechanical, structural cause — seclusio pupillae.

answers.text: Neovascularisation of the angle (rubeosis iridis) from posterior segment ischaemia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Rubeosis iridis causes neovascular glaucoma, which is not associated with 360° posterior synechiae or iris bombé in the typical sequence. The clinical picture here (seclusio + bowing) is classic for pupil-block glaucoma.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: seclusio pupillae means aqueous cannot pass through the pupil. It pools behind the iris, forcing it forward (bombé) and closing the angle. Treatment requires re-establishing the pupillary passage — laser iridotomy or surgical iridectomy.
Excellent. Seclusio pupillae → aqueous trapped behind iris → iris bombé → secondary angle closure. This chain is a high-yield exam scenario.
